stance_summary: Methodologist: do not commit to a 40-学时 大纲 until a cheapest-possible diagnostic disambiguates which floor (math, coding, modeling, AI-literacy, project-mgmt) actually binds for incoming Tongji 大二 physics students.
anchored_assumption: We do not know whether the binding bottleneck for these students is H3 MODELING (cannot translate a physical scene into variables / equations) or H2 CODING (every code lesson burns half the block on syntax+env before any physics lands); the two competing hypotheses imply opposite curricula, and both T1 and T2 silently picked one without testing. A secondary disambiguation is H3 vs H4 (over-trust in AI outputs) since the course title forces AI use.

candidates.one_line: Run a 4-hour single-afternoon diagnostic clinic with 6-8 current 大一-末 physics students this week, using one fixed physics scene (damped pendulum from rest, released at 30 degrees, with air drag), to measure where they actually break: modeling, coding, or AI-trust.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today: post a WeChat-group recruitment for 6-8 大一 physics volunteers for a paid 4-hour Saturday session; draft the single-page diagnostic protocol with three timed stations: Station 1 (45 min, no computer, pencil only): write down the variables, write the ODE, sketch expected x(t). Station 2 (90 min, laptop + Cursor/Claude allowed): produce a numerical x(t) plot and one quantitative claim about decay time. Station 3 (45 min, debrief): student is shown a deliberately wrong AI-generated solution where the sign of the drag term is flipped, asked to find the error in 20 minutes; record whether they catch it, how, and how long.
candidates.cost_estimate: Instructor time: 6 h prep (write protocol, prepare wrong-sign trap code, print worksheets) + 4 h running + 2 h scoring = 12 instructor-hours total, one weekend. Zero compute. Pizza budget ~300 RMB.
candidates.info_gain: Pass: if median student clears Station 1 cleanly but stalls at Station 2 -> H2 (coding floor) confirmed, curriculum must front-load env+syntax via AI scaffolding. If they stall at Station 1 -> H3 (modeling floor), curriculum must spend Days 1-3 on translating-scenes-to-equations with pencil-only exercises. If they sail through 1 and 2 but miss the sign-flip in Station 3 -> H4 (AI-trust floor), curriculum must center AI-output critique. Fail (no clear pattern across 6-8 students): tells you the cohort is heterogeneous and Day 1 must be a forking placement track. Either branch is decisive input for the 大纲.
candidates.risk: 8 volunteers is not statistically representative; could mislead if you happen to draw the top 8 of the class. Mitigation: actively recruit a mix including students who self-report struggling with 大一 普物.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T1. Course shell modeled as 32 学时 / 16 sessions x 2 学时, framed as undergraduate research-method training for general physics undergraduates.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T1 is a final-design commitment with no measurement; B1 is a 12-hour empirical probe that produces no syllabus and instead generates the input data the syllabus must be conditioned on.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T2. 40 学时 / 10 教学日 / 4-phase 大纲 with RK4 / SymPy / FFT / MC / Bootstrap as core content tower.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T2 silently assumed the binding constraint was content-level mismatch (and proposed advanced numerics); B1 refuses to pick the level before measuring which of three orthogonal floors actually breaks first on a single concrete physics task.

dependencies: 6-8 大一 physics volunteers reachable via existing Tongji channels
one shared laptop room or BYOD with Cursor/Claude access pre-installed
one wrong-sign-trap reference code (instructor writes in ~1 hour)
a 1-page scoring rubric (pencil grade, code grade, AI-critique grade)

candidates.one_line: Adopt MIT 8.S50 / Rice 'Vibe Coding for Research' as a known-solved subproblem skeleton, but reduce it to a 1-day port: pick exactly ONE of their published modules, run it as-is with a Tongji 大二-incoming student tomorrow, and only if it lands cleanly does it earn a slot in the 10-day syllabus.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today: open the MIT 8.S50 (Computational Physics) and Rice Ken Kennedy Institute 'AI for Physicists' public materials, identify the single shortest self-contained module that takes a freshman from 'physical scene' to 'numerical plot' in under 3 hours of student time (candidate: the 1D heat-equation or coupled-oscillator notebook), download it, then walk through it tomorrow morning with ONE 大二-incoming student over Zoom while screen-recording. Score the recording on a 5-item rubric: did they understand the physics setup / did the code run on first try / did they explain the plot in their own words / did they spot an injected bug / did they finish in budget.
candidates.cost_estimate: 4 hours instructor prep (find module, inject one bug, write rubric) + 3 hours running with one student + 1 hour postmortem = 8 instructor-hours total, one day. Zero compute. Zero RMB.
candidates.info_gain: Pass: the imported module lands -> Tongji 大一 audience is within the range of an established freshman-level computational-physics module, and you can build the 10-day course as 4-5 such modules stitched together, each pre-validated. Fail: the module does NOT land -> you have positive evidence that even MIT-freshman-calibrated material is too hard for the Tongji 大一-末 audience, which is itself a strong constraint (rules out N existing curricula, forces ground-up design). Either branch shrinks the design space.
candidates.risk: n=1 student is noise-limited; the chosen module may not be representative of the imported curriculum as a whole. Mitigation: stratified — pick the module the importing curriculum advertises as its EASIEST first week, so a failure there is informative.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T1. Course shell modeled as 32 学时 / 16 sessions x 2 学时, framed as undergraduate research-method training for general physics undergraduates.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T1 invented a shell from scratch with no external calibration; B2 forces calibration against a publicly documented, already-piloted curriculum before any local design starts.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T2. 40 学时 / 10 教学日 / 4-phase 大纲 with RK4 / SymPy / FFT / MC / Bootstrap as core content tower.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T2 chose its content tower from the instructor's own research toolbox; B2 chooses content from a known-solved-elsewhere subproblem and tests one slice before importing the rest.

dependencies: public MIT 8.S50 and Rice Vibe Coding materials (already on the open web, no access barrier)
one volunteer 大一-末 student reachable in 24 hours
Zoom or equivalent with screen recording
no new software for the instructor

candidates.one_line: Ablation pilot: design Day 1 of the course as a self-contained 4-学时 standalone workshop with a pass/fail end-of-day milestone, teach it once to 8 students, and only proceed to Days 2-10 if the milestone is hit by the median student.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today: write a single Day-1 lesson plan on a single page with this success criterion verbatim — 'By 17:00, every student has (a) produced a x(t) plot of ideal projectile motion they can defend in 60 seconds; (b) produced a second plot with air drag added by editing the same script with AI assistance; (c) identified ONE numerical or physical error in an AI-generated variant the instructor injected.' Then write the 4 lesson blocks (45 min each) that lead to that criterion: Block 1 pencil derivation of equations of motion, Block 2 AI-assisted first plot from scratch, Block 3 add a physical complication, Block 4 critique an injected wrong answer. The first concrete action today is writing this single page and the four blocks; the pilot itself is scheduled for next week.
candidates.cost_estimate: Day-1 design: 4 instructor-hours today. Pilot delivery: 4 h teach + 2 h debrief = 6 hours next weekend with 8 volunteers. Total: 10 instructor-hours to either green-light the rest of the 大纲 or stop and redesign. Zero compute.
candidates.info_gain: Pass: median student hits all three milestones -> the chosen pacing (1 day = 1 scene from pencil to AI-critiqued plot) is calibrated, and Days 2-10 inherit the same template: one scene per day, escalating physical complexity (Day 2 oscillators, Day 3 coupled oscillators, Day 4 heat / diffusion, ...) with the AI-critique slot held constant. Fail: criterion missed -> the 1-day-per-scene pacing is too aggressive and the unit must be widened to 2 days per scene, immediately cutting the syllabus from 10 scenes to 5 (informative). Either way you learn the right TIME-PER-CONCEPT constant before committing 40 hours of content design.
candidates.risk: Conflates two variables: pacing AND content choice. If projectile-with-drag is a bad choice, you cannot tell if pacing failed or the example failed. Mitigation: replicate with one alternate scene (damped pendulum) in the same pilot if you have a second cohort slot.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T1. Course shell modeled as 32 学时 / 16 sessions x 2 学时, framed as undergraduate research-method training for general physics undergraduates.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T1 fixes a global shell with no per-day success criterion; B3 reverses the order — defines the day-1 unit-test first, runs it, then induces the shell from what worked.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T2. 40 学时 / 10 教学日 / 4-phase 大纲 with RK4 / SymPy / FFT / MC / Bootstrap as core content tower.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T2 commits to 4 thematic phases without testing per-day pacing; B3 tests exactly one day in isolation as the smallest replicable unit and refuses to scale up until the unit holds.

dependencies: projectile-with-drag is a 大一-普物 topic so no new physics required from instructor
AI tool (Claude or Cursor) account access
an injected-error reference script (~30 min to write)

candidates.one_line: Strip the course to its weakest defensible ablation — no AI, no Python, no projects, only pencil-and-spreadsheet modeling of 8 physical scenes over 10 days — and use the pilot of Day 1 of THAT design as a null hypothesis: if students cannot build a damped-oscillator spreadsheet model in 4 hours, no AI tool will save the course.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today: write the alternative-null Day-1 plan on one page — students model a damped harmonic oscillator in Excel/WPS only, using Euler stepping in adjacent rows, then plot x vs t, vary the damping coefficient, and answer a written question: 'at what damping does the system stop oscillating?'. Success criterion: median student produces the plot AND correctly identifies the critical-damping boundary by 17:00. Then schedule this as the diagnostic for next Saturday alongside or instead of B3.
candidates.cost_estimate: Design: 3 instructor-hours today (Excel template + answer key + 1-page worksheet). Pilot: 4 h teach + 1 h debrief = 5 h. Total: 8 instructor-hours. Zero compute, zero software install.
candidates.info_gain: Pass: students CAN build a numerical physics model when the tool friction is near-zero (spreadsheet) -> the binding constraint is NOT modeling (H3 falsified) and the AI/Python layer is purely about scale, not about whether they can think. The 大纲 then justifiably commits to AI+Python from Day 2 onward. Fail: students cannot even do the spreadsheet version -> the binding constraint IS modeling (H3 confirmed), and adding AI on top of a broken modeling habit will produce confident-looking-but-wrong outputs all course long. In that case, Days 1-4 of the real course MUST be spreadsheet-only modeling before any AI is introduced. This is the single highest-information experiment in the design space because it cleanly separates H2 from H3.
candidates.risk: Spreadsheet is unfamiliar to physicists and may itself add friction, polluting the signal. Mitigation: pre-fill the Excel template with row labels and the time column so the student only writes the recurrence formula.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T1. Course shell modeled as 32 学时 / 16 sessions x 2 学时, framed as undergraduate research-method training for general physics undergraduates.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T1 assumed students need a research-method scaffold; B4 strips away all scaffolding to test whether the underlying modeling capacity exists at all.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T2. 40 学时 / 10 教学日 / 4-phase 大纲 with RK4 / SymPy / FFT / MC / Bootstrap as core content tower.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T2 makes the unstated assumption that AI+Python is necessary to teach modeling; B4 actively tests the opposite assumption (modeling habit transferable through spreadsheets), making the AI layer falsifiable rather than load-bearing-by-fiat.

dependencies: Excel / WPS on student laptops (already installed everywhere in Chinese university context)
8 volunteer students for one Saturday afternoon
a pre-filled Excel template (~1 hour to build)
the instructor only needs to know Excel formulas — no new tools

candidates.one_line: Define the course-level success criterion FIRST as a published artifact rubric (what every group's Day-10 deliverable must demonstrate), then pilot only the rubric-grading step today against a hand-fabricated 'good' and 'bad' student artifact to verify the rubric discriminates before any teaching is designed.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today: write the course-end-deliverable rubric on one page with 5 binary items, e.g. (1) the artifact states the physical scene in 3 sentences using only 大一-普物 vocabulary; (2) the equations of motion are derived on paper and photographed into the report; (3) at least one numerical plot is produced with AI-assisted code AND the student annotates ONE prompt they had to reject; (4) the deliverable contains one cross-check (analytical limit, dimensional check, or comparison to a textbook value); (5) a 60-second video explanation a 大一 classmate can follow. Then fabricate two artifacts yourself in 3 hours — one designed to pass, one designed to fail on items 3 and 4 — and have a colleague blind-grade them with the rubric. Confirm rubric discriminates 5/5 vs 2/5 before any pedagogy is designed.
candidates.cost_estimate: 3 h rubric draft + 3 h fabricate two artifacts + 1 h blind co-grade with second instructor = 7 instructor-hours, today. Zero student involvement at this stage.
candidates.info_gain: Pass: the rubric distinguishes the planted good from the planted bad cleanly -> you have a defensible, examinable assessment instrument, and the entire 10-day syllabus design becomes a backward induction from this rubric (every day's lesson must explicitly produce evidence for at least one rubric item). Fail: rubric does not discriminate or co-instructor disagrees on scoring -> the course's intended outcome is not yet operationally defined, and you have caught this before writing the syllabus rather than at the end. Without B5 passing, B1-B4 grade against an undefined target.
candidates.risk: Designing the rubric before piloting students risks making it instructor-aspirational rather than student-achievable. Mitigation: explicitly cross-reference each rubric item to 大一-普物 vocabulary only, and treat B5 as a precondition to be revised after B1 / B3 / B4 land empirical data.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T1. Course shell modeled as 32 学时 / 16 sessions x 2 学时, framed as undergraduate research-method training for general physics undergraduates.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T1 specified an assessment weighting (50/20/15/10/5) but not what a passing artifact actually looks like; B5 demands the artifact spec exist and discriminate before any session count is fixed.

orthogonality_to_tried.tried_item: T2. 40 学时 / 10 教学日 / 4-phase 大纲 with RK4 / SymPy / FFT / MC / Bootstrap as core content tower.
orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T2 designed content top-down from method categories; B5 designs bottom-up from the artifact-level evidence the course must produce, decoupling the assessment-correctness check from any pedagogical commitment.

dependencies: second instructor available for 1 hour of blind co-grading
no students needed at this stage
no AI tool needed at this stage (the rubric is paper-only)

convergence_note: Solver A (contrarian) is likely to independently propose something resembling B4 (radical ablation: drop the AI / drop the Python) and possibly B2 (import an external curriculum). Solver A is unlikely to propose B1 (multi-station diagnostic clinic with explicit H2/H3/H4 fork), B3 (Day-1-as-unit-test), or B5 (rubric-before-syllabus), because those are experimental-design moves rather than contrarian moves on the curriculum's content.
